title: Induction and finite histories in Peano arithmetic

based_on.title: Provability logic: models within models in Peano Arithmetic
An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Induction inside arithmetic constructs coded histories at every internal length.
abstract: An ordinary finite computation has a list of intermediate values. To reason about every input in Peano arithmetic, we need the same construction at the lengths that occur inside any of its models. We begin with induction for formulas with parameters, derive division and the elementary congruence argument, and use them to append a value to a coded history. The proof keeps an explicit arithmetic invariant at each stage. This also explains how a bounded family of individually available witnesses can be collected into one code, without assuming an external list of nonstandard length.
